title: Cybersecurity Daily Briefing
description: Actively exploited vulnerabilities, major incidents, and threat trends relevant to enterprise and federal networks.
readFirst: Covers Oct. 20–23. The patching priority is Arista's Oct. 22 advisory: CVE-2026-114625 in on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator is being exploited. Amazon says a PHP2Shell attempt hit a honeypot on Oct. 17, before the Oct. 21 disclosure; CISA had not reported exploitation when it issued that alert. The Oct. 20 KEV batch and the Cisco Snort advisory were dropped because they are no longer the current patching priority. No new CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog addition was posted for Oct. 22 or Oct. 23. CISA did publish an Industrial Edge Device Kit advisory on Oct. 22. No new public update on the DMDC personnel breach was found.

items.headline: Arista says an exploited VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw lets a read-only user become a superuser operator
items.summary: Arista's Security Advisory 0199, dated Oct. 22, covers CVE-2026-114625, a SQL injection in on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator that Arista scores at 9.9 in CVSS 3.1. Arista says any authenticated user, including the Enterprise Read Only role, can gain operator privileges and masquerade as a local superuser operator, and that the flaw is known to be actively exploited. Hosted and Dedicated orchestrators are already patched. Arista says VeloCloud Gateway and VeloCloud Edge are not affected, names 74.82.197.86 and 38.54.50.151 as addresses seen in the attacks, and gives the on-premises fixes as VCO 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10, and 6.4.2.12 and later.

items.headline: Amazon saw PHP2Shell attempts four days before the patch; CISA had not reported exploitation
items.summary: CISA said Oct. 21 that CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which it calls php2shell, allow unauthenticated remote code execution on PHP installations that serve web requests, and that it had not observed exploitation as of the alert. CISA told organizations to update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, or 8.2.35, and to take PHP 8.1 and earlier offline if they cannot update. Amazon Threat Intelligence wrote the same day that its MadPot honeypot recorded an exploitation attempt on Oct. 17, four days before public disclosure, from an address on a commercial anonymization network, and that further attempts on the morning of Oct. 21 came from multiple actors. Amazon said it is unclear whether those attempts would have worked on real systems, and that after the patch PHP2Shell was seeing broad exploitation attempts.

items.headline: Microsoft says Storm-0940 used an AI pentest framework in the ConnectWise compromise
items.summary: Microsoft said Oct. 21 that Storm-0940, which it describes as a China-state-aligned actor, used the open-source agentic penetration-testing framework ARTEX and was responsible for the ConnectWise multi-tenant application compromise. After that access, Microsoft said, the actor used ARTEX to attempt sign-ins to more than 2,250 tenants at 2,900 attempts per minute, and in multiple cases reached privileged cloud access in under three hours. Microsoft said the activity did not come from a flaw in Microsoft's own products, and that an affected application or a successful sign-in does not by itself mean customer data was taken. Its guidance is to keep the affected ConnectWise application connections disabled until ConnectWise publishes restoration instructions, and to review activity from at least Oct. 15.

items.headline: SafePay advisory: about 600 victims, initial access through edge devices and stolen passwords
items.summary: CISA, the FBI, the Secret Service and international partners released a StopRansomware advisory on SafePay dated Oct. 20. A CISA news release the next day says the group has hit about 600 victims across the Americas, Europe and Australia and is one of the most active ransomware groups of 2026. Actors steal or guess passwords, use phishing, and exploit known vulnerabilities on internet-facing devices, often arriving through VPN. They then create or take over accounts, move with legitimate admin tools, disable backups, steal data and encrypt systems. Listed exploited bugs in the advisory include CVE-2020-3259, CVE-2023-20269, CVE-2023-27532, CVE-2024-40711 and CVE-2024-40766. CISA's ask is to patch edge devices, require multifactor authentication, restrict admin tools, segment networks and keep offline backups that have been restored in a test.

items.headline: CISA: path traversal in Siemens Industrial Edge Device Kit can expose internal data
items.summary: CISA published ICSA-26-295-09 on Oct. 22 for the Siemens Industrial Edge Device Kit. CISA says multiple path-traversal flaws, CVE-2026-44414 and CVE-2026-44415, could let an authenticated remote attacker reach sensitive internal information. The advisory lists a CVSS v3 score of 9.1 and says Siemens has released new versions for several affected products and recommends countermeasures where a fix is not yet available. The advisory does not say these flaws are being exploited.

items.headline: OpenAI commits $1 billion in model access for defenders after the PHP find
items.summary: In the same Oct. 21 post on the PHP flaws, OpenAI said it has committed $1 billion in subsidized Daybreak access for organizations with limited security resources that protect essential services. It said that, to its knowledge, frontier AI found the PHP bugs before attackers did, and that the same capabilities can help attackers build exploits. OpenAI said it worked with partners to engage CISA, the Office of the National Cyber Director, and what it called the White House's Super Intelligence Force, plus international partners, before the public disclosure. It also published a five-stage proposal for how maintainers, providers, and government agencies should handle the next bug of this scale.
